nodes.title: Revisions
nodes.body: 8/13/93. T.D. Phillips; Mote Marine Laboratory, Sarasota, FL.

nodes.title: TAXONOMY
nodes.body:
Common Name: Gulf flounder
Scientific Name: Paralichthys albigutta

nodes.title: Classification
nodes.body:
Phylum: Chordata
      Class: Osteichthyes
      Order: Pleuronectiformes
      Family: Paralichthyidae

Other Common Names:  lenguado panzablanca (Spanish) sand flounder (13761), flounder (664 834 13761, fluke (232)

nodes.title: VALUE & STATUS
nodes.body:
Commercial: Gulf flounder are not the focus of a directed fishery. They are caught mainly with trawls and often form part of the by-catch of commercial shrimpers (47). When marketed, they are usually sold fresh or frozen (791). Separate catch statistics are not maintained for the species and they are lumped with other species as “flounder” (791 902). Flounder landings for all of Florida were 413,665 lbs in 1989 (902).

Recreational: Gulf flounder are caught by sport fishermen primarily using hook-and-line baited with live, fresh or frozen baits. (232). No estimates of the recreational catch are available.

Ecological Role: No information found

Indicator: No information found

nodes.title: GEOGRAPHIC RANGE
nodes.body:
Overall:  Coastal waters from Cape Lookout, North Carolina to at least south Texas, and in the western Bahamas (327 729 788 871 891 1376). Fischer (791) also includes the western Caribbean as part of its range.

Within Study Area: In the Gulf of Mexico, gulf flounder are common from South Florida to Perdido Bay (729 983). Occurs along the entire Atlantic coast of Florida and around peninsular Florida; greatest numbers occur on the Florida west coast (729).

Mobility and Migration:
Adults migrate out of the estuaries to neritic offshore waters during fall and winter to spawn. Timing of the movement is associated with the advent of falling water temperatures (677). Beginning in late spring to early summer the adults and juveniles return to the estuarine habitats (232 581 664 677). Only one tagging study has been done (677), but only 33 individuals were tagged and there were no tag returns.

nodes.title: Life Mode
nodes.body: Eggs and larvae are planktonic. Postlarvae become demersal, after metamorphosis; juveniles and adults are demersal (232).

nodes.title: Habitat Type
nodes.body:
Eggs:  are marine and neritic.
Larvae: are marine and neritic, becoming estuarine.
Juveniles: are estuarine and marine.
Adults: are estuarine and neritic, but prefer shallow Gulf waters (470). Springer and Woodburn (664) collected juveniles and adults in all types of habitats in Tampa Bay, including grassbeds. Spadefish have also been collected on the rocky reefs offshore of Tampa Bay (7981, and occasionally around coral reefs in the extreme western Bahamas (871).

Substrate: Gulf flounder typically occur over hard, sand bottoms (327 499 677 7911, but they are also found over sand-mud or strictly mud bottoms (499). Juveniles have been reported in association with seagrass beds (327 581 664 677).

nodes.title: Physical/Chemical
nodes.body:
Temperature: The reported range of temperatures for Gulf flounder is from 2-4 C to 32.5 C (581 664 769). Stokes (677) reported that Gulf flounder in Texas moved offshore when water temperatures fell from 23 in October to 14.1 C in December; and that peak immigration of juveniles back into the estuaries occurred at temperatures around 16 C. In Florida, they have been collected at temperatures of 8.3 to 30.6 C at Cedar Key (378 5811, 11.2 to 32-50 C in Tampa Bay (664), 19.0 to 27.8 C in Everglades National Park (1373), 23.0 to 28.0 C at Matecumbe Key (800), and 20.0 to 28.0 C at Jupiter Inlet (887) .

Salinity: Gulf flounder range from the seawater zone to the upper end of the mixing zone. The reported salinity range is 6-60 ppt (566 677). They reportedly prefer salinities greater than 20 ppt (566 581 664 677). Salinity ranges for Florida collections are: 17.5-31.5% at Cedar Key (378 5811, 13.7-33.7% at Tampa Bay (6641, 22.3-35.4% at Everglades National Park (13731, 35.1-37.9% at Matecumbe Key (800), and 33.5-35.4% at Jupiter Inlet (887). Williams and Deubler (769) reported that postlarvae are found in estuarine habitats at salinities at or greater than 22 ppt.

Turbidity: Stokes (677) stated gulf flounder were not present in waters with turbidity greater than 65 J.T.U.

nodes.title: REPRODUCTION
nodes.body:
Reproductive Mode: Sexes are separate. Oviparous, fertilization occurs within the water column following broadcasting of gametes. The eggs float at or near the surface of the water (232).

Mating/Spawning: Spawning occurs during late fall and early winter (Nov-Feb) in marine neritic waters (232 677). Specimens with ripe gonads collected in 20-40m in the eastern Gulf in Nov-Feb (729). Spent females have been collected in Tampa Bay in February (729). Females are sexually mature by age 11, and at a size as small as 245mm TL (499 1014).

Fecundity: No data on fecundity available (232).

nodes.title: Length Range
nodes.body:
Egg: Data related to egg description, time of hatching, and period of early larval development are lacking.
Larvae: appear in the eastern Gulf of Mexico from December through early March.
Postlarvae: range in size from 7-10 mm SL, average 8.4 mm. Growth at least up to 50 mm appears to be rapid (499 232).
Adults: Stokes (677) calculated growth rates up to two years in males: (0) 10-220 mm TL, .15 kg, (I) 221-290 mm, .27 kg; and up to three years for females: (0) 10-290 mm TL, .27 kg, (I) 291-360, .57 kg, (11) 361-420 mm TL, 1.01 kg. Average size of two year old fish reported as 350mm TL, and of 3 year old fish 400mm TL (1014).

Other: Length-weight relationships determined for North Carolina gulf flounder (615) are (sexes combined):

[eq]
logw = -5.24 + 3.134 log 1 r = 0.97
[/eq]

females only:

[eq]
log w = -5.018 + 3.053 log 1 r = 0.955, n = 62
[/eq]

Females live only 3 years and males 2 years, although actual life spans probably exceed three years (232). Maturation occurs around 145 mm SL for females (729). Stokes noted ripe females were two years old and stated that females grow more rapidly and attain greater sizes than males. Largest female examined by Stokes (677) was 420mm TL and the largest male was 290mm TL. The maximum reported size is 710 mm TL, 5 kg appears to be based on a misidentified individual (232).

nodes.title: FOOD HABITS
nodes.body: Small gulf flounder, 10-50 mm TL, feed predominantly on invertebrates mostly crustaceans, especially mysids and amphipods (581). Juvenile Gulf flounder consume both small fish and crustaceans, including penaeid shrimp and portunid crabs (232 677). At 100-150 mm TL they are primarily piscivorous (567 581 664 677 729). Noted prey include Brevoortia sp., Anchoa mitchilli, Anchoa sp., Synodus foetens, Fundulus similis, Syngnathus sp., Haemulon sp., Orthopristis chrysoptera, Lagodon rhomboides, Micropognias undulatus, Mugil sp. and Gobiosoma robustum as well as a number of unidentified forms (47 532 581 664 677 729).

sections.heading: HEADER
sections.content:
Title: Gulf Flounder (Paralichthys albigutta)

FLELMR Code: 2990

sections.heading: Revisions
sections.content: 8/13/93. T.D. Phillips; Mote Marine Laboratory, Sarasota, FL.

sections.heading: TAXONOMY
sections.content:
Common Name: Gulf flounder
Scientific Name: Paralichthys albigutta

sections.heading: Classification
sections.content:
Phylum: Chordata
      Class: Osteichthyes
      Order: Pleuronectiformes
      Family: Paralichthyidae

Other Common Names:  lenguado panzablanca (Spanish) sand flounder (13761), flounder (664 834 13761, fluke (232)

sections.heading: VALUE & STATUS
sections.content:
Commercial: Gulf flounder are not the focus of a directed fishery. They are caught mainly with trawls and often form part of the by-catch of commercial shrimpers (47). When marketed, they are usually sold fresh or frozen (791). Separate catch statistics are not maintained for the species and they are lumped with other species as “flounder” (791 902). Flounder landings for all of Florida were 413,665 lbs in 1989 (902).

Recreational: Gulf flounder are caught by sport fishermen primarily using hook-and-line baited with live, fresh or frozen baits. (232). No estimates of the recreational catch are available.

Ecological Role: No information found

Indicator: No information found

sections.heading: GEOGRAPHIC RANGE
sections.content:
Overall:  Coastal waters from Cape Lookout, North Carolina to at least south Texas, and in the western Bahamas (327 729 788 871 891 1376). Fischer (791) also includes the western Caribbean as part of its range.

Within Study Area: In the Gulf of Mexico, gulf flounder are common from South Florida to Perdido Bay (729 983). Occurs along the entire Atlantic coast of Florida and around peninsular Florida; greatest numbers occur on the Florida west coast (729).

Mobility and Migration:
Adults migrate out of the estuaries to neritic offshore waters during fall and winter to spawn. Timing of the movement is associated with the advent of falling water temperatures (677). Beginning in late spring to early summer the adults and juveniles return to the estuarine habitats (232 581 664 677). Only one tagging study has been done (677), but only 33 individuals were tagged and there were no tag returns.

sections.heading: Life Mode
sections.content: Eggs and larvae are planktonic. Postlarvae become demersal, after metamorphosis; juveniles and adults are demersal (232).

sections.heading: Habitat Type
sections.content:
Eggs:  are marine and neritic.
Larvae: are marine and neritic, becoming estuarine.
Juveniles: are estuarine and marine.
Adults: are estuarine and neritic, but prefer shallow Gulf waters (470). Springer and Woodburn (664) collected juveniles and adults in all types of habitats in Tampa Bay, including grassbeds. Spadefish have also been collected on the rocky reefs offshore of Tampa Bay (7981, and occasionally around coral reefs in the extreme western Bahamas (871).

Substrate: Gulf flounder typically occur over hard, sand bottoms (327 499 677 7911, but they are also found over sand-mud or strictly mud bottoms (499). Juveniles have been reported in association with seagrass beds (327 581 664 677).

sections.heading: Physical/Chemical
sections.content:
Temperature: The reported range of temperatures for Gulf flounder is from 2-4 C to 32.5 C (581 664 769). Stokes (677) reported that Gulf flounder in Texas moved offshore when water temperatures fell from 23 in October to 14.1 C in December; and that peak immigration of juveniles back into the estuaries occurred at temperatures around 16 C. In Florida, they have been collected at temperatures of 8.3 to 30.6 C at Cedar Key (378 5811, 11.2 to 32-50 C in Tampa Bay (664), 19.0 to 27.8 C in Everglades National Park (1373), 23.0 to 28.0 C at Matecumbe Key (800), and 20.0 to 28.0 C at Jupiter Inlet (887) .

Salinity: Gulf flounder range from the seawater zone to the upper end of the mixing zone. The reported salinity range is 6-60 ppt (566 677). They reportedly prefer salinities greater than 20 ppt (566 581 664 677). Salinity ranges for Florida collections are: 17.5-31.5% at Cedar Key (378 5811, 13.7-33.7% at Tampa Bay (6641, 22.3-35.4% at Everglades National Park (13731, 35.1-37.9% at Matecumbe Key (800), and 33.5-35.4% at Jupiter Inlet (887). Williams and Deubler (769) reported that postlarvae are found in estuarine habitats at salinities at or greater than 22 ppt.

Turbidity: Stokes (677) stated gulf flounder were not present in waters with turbidity greater than 65 J.T.U.

sections.heading: REPRODUCTION
sections.content:
Reproductive Mode: Sexes are separate. Oviparous, fertilization occurs within the water column following broadcasting of gametes. The eggs float at or near the surface of the water (232).

Mating/Spawning: Spawning occurs during late fall and early winter (Nov-Feb) in marine neritic waters (232 677). Specimens with ripe gonads collected in 20-40m in the eastern Gulf in Nov-Feb (729). Spent females have been collected in Tampa Bay in February (729). Females are sexually mature by age 11, and at a size as small as 245mm TL (499 1014).

Fecundity: No data on fecundity available (232).

sections.heading: Length Range
sections.content:
Egg: Data related to egg description, time of hatching, and period of early larval development are lacking.
Larvae: appear in the eastern Gulf of Mexico from December through early March.
Postlarvae: range in size from 7-10 mm SL, average 8.4 mm. Growth at least up to 50 mm appears to be rapid (499 232).
Adults: Stokes (677) calculated growth rates up to two years in males: (0) 10-220 mm TL, .15 kg, (I) 221-290 mm, .27 kg; and up to three years for females: (0) 10-290 mm TL, .27 kg, (I) 291-360, .57 kg, (11) 361-420 mm TL, 1.01 kg. Average size of two year old fish reported as 350mm TL, and of 3 year old fish 400mm TL (1014).

Other: Length-weight relationships determined for North Carolina gulf flounder (615) are (sexes combined):

[eq]
logw = -5.24 + 3.134 log 1 r = 0.97
[/eq]

females only:

[eq]
log w = -5.018 + 3.053 log 1 r = 0.955, n = 62
[/eq]

Females live only 3 years and males 2 years, although actual life spans probably exceed three years (232). Maturation occurs around 145 mm SL for females (729). Stokes noted ripe females were two years old and stated that females grow more rapidly and attain greater sizes than males. Largest female examined by Stokes (677) was 420mm TL and the largest male was 290mm TL. The maximum reported size is 710 mm TL, 5 kg appears to be based on a misidentified individual (232).

sections.heading: FOOD HABITS
sections.content: Small gulf flounder, 10-50 mm TL, feed predominantly on invertebrates mostly crustaceans, especially mysids and amphipods (581). Juvenile Gulf flounder consume both small fish and crustaceans, including penaeid shrimp and portunid crabs (232 677). At 100-150 mm TL they are primarily piscivorous (567 581 664 677 729). Noted prey include Brevoortia sp., Anchoa mitchilli, Anchoa sp., Synodus foetens, Fundulus similis, Syngnathus sp., Haemulon sp., Orthopristis chrysoptera, Lagodon rhomboides, Micropognias undulatus, Mugil sp. and Gobiosoma robustum as well as a number of unidentified forms (47 532 581 664 677 729).
